text:
alex: FYI customer reported big p95/p99 jump after the runtime push last night. ACME says chat endpoints slow and some requests 500-ing. Anyone watching infra dashboards?

deploy-bot: rollout v6.3 -> promoted to 80% at 22:14 UTC, 23:05 UTC last night. No automated rollback triggered.

maya: I see a correlated p99 increase on the runtime host pool around 22:30->23:20 UTC. p50 unchanged. Looks like tail latency, likely queuing.

raj: Auth path shows increased latency too. Token fetch p99 went from 40ms -> 1.2s in the same window. Could be upstream fanout with a new kernel path.

alex: good call. customer logs include: ```ERR auth: timeout fetching token (deadline exceeded) host=auth-1.prod```. They also saw 502s when auth timed out.

sam-csm: ACME is hitting us with a support escalation — they have an interactive product, so 1s p99 is breaking UX. They're also worried about billing spikes (tons of retries).

ella: any downstream change to token refresh strategy in the rollout? we recently changed token caching TTL for the runtime to favor fresh tokens.

maya: yes, v6.3 flipped token cache window to 0s for safety with tenant-scoped keys (we did that in canary). That multiplies token fetches per request. If the auth service had a small capacity dip, it amplifies tail.

raj: hypothesis: rollout changed auth cache semantics + new kernel scheduler induced small queuing -> auth fanout + slower kvcache = p99. We should bisect between (a) kernel scheduler change and (b) token cache TTL flip.

alex: repro steps from ACME: ```curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <shortlived>" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/responses -d '{"prompt":"hello"}' -v```  — with v6.3 we see ~800ms on auth and total 1200-1500ms. On previous runtime image it's ~120ms.

ops-oncall: mitigation plan: 1) throttle token refreshes by re-enabling cache TTL (quick patch to agents) 2) roll back kernel scheduler on a subset of hosts 3) route 10% of traffic back to v6.2 while we bisect. Recommend doing 1) immediately.

ella: I'll open a fast rollback PR to restore token cache for the runtime agents (hotfix). Patch is small, should be deployable to canary in ~10m.

maya: I'll carve out a canary cohort and re-route 10% traffic to v6.2 now. Creating routing change.

raj: I'll run bisect tests: spin up two small clusters (v6.3 w/TTL=0, v6.3 w/TTL=old, v6.2) and run synthetic workload that exercises auth per request and long sequence lengths to reproduce queuing. Sharing repro harness in 15m.

sam-csm: please flag me when we have the first canary rollback / mitigation so I can update ACME support thread. They want ETA and whether billing will be rebated.

alex: quick note — instrument a sampling trace that includes auth latency, kernel-scheduler label, and token-cache-hit boolean. Need to prove which change dominates.

deploy-bot: rollback route change applied: cohort-3 -> v6.2 (10%). Canary deploy of token-cache-hotfix promoted to 5% canary.

ops-oncall: monitoring: p99 dropped from 1.2s -> 360ms in the cohort routed back to v6.2. Canary with cache hotfix also trending down (~400ms). Good signs.

ella: patch merged and promoted to 30% canary. Opening an incident doc for tracking and RCA.

raj: preliminary bisect result: token-cache TTL flip alone reproduces >80% of the p99 delta. Kernel scheduler tweak adds ~40ms but not the 800-1000ms jump.

alex: conclusion: primary root cause = token cache TTL change + auth service pressure amplifying queuing; kernel change is secondary amplifier. Action items: (1) keep token cache hotfix rolled out to 100% (ella) (2) schedule kernel scheduler rollback/soft-penalty tuning in next maintenance window (maya/infra) (3) add circuit-breaker to token fetch with cached fallback to avoid auth-fanout on failure (raj/serving).

sam-csm: ACME updated. They want an incident postmortem and to know if we will rebate retry charges. I'm looping legal/finance.

ops-oncall: closing thread for active mitigation; will update incident doc as RCA and timeline fleshed out. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
